newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: TENNIS-SAMPRAS WINS FIRST MATCH SINCE U.S. OPEN TRIUMPH.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS WINS FIRST MATCH SINCE U.S. OPEN TRIUMPH.

text.p: Pete Sampras returned to work on Wednesday in his first match since winning the U.S. Open by beating Alex Radulescu at the Swiss indoor championships.
The world number one dropped the first set against the German qualifier before fighting back to win 5-7 6-3 7-5.
"I took a good week and a half off after the Open and didn't pick up a racquet," said Sampras. "Last Wednesday I starting hitting few balls.
"I guess maybe a lack of matches contributed to the slow start."
The big-serving Radulescu, who reached the quarter-finals at Wimbledon this year, took the first set after breaking Sampras in the first game.
Sampras took the second set then showed the stuff of champions in the third.
Serving at 4-3, down 15-40 he clawed back with four winners to prevent a potentially crucial break.

"One big swing there and he could have won," said Sampras, making his first appearance in Switzerland since an exhibition against Ivan Lendl six years ago. "But I had a couple of good shots and I'm still here.
"I could have just as easily missed one of those shots but I didn't. In the second and third sets I was starting to get in a pretty good groove and now I hope I can maintain it.
"In the third set I pulled a couple of shots out the bag."

Sampras was never able to take control of the match as Radulescu, ranked 62nd in the world, made the winner of eight grand slam titles work for every point in a match that lasted two hours three minutes.
"He's a big server and he's been playing well," said Sampras. "He's very capable of beating me and he nearly did."
Third seed Yevgeny Kafelnikov of Russia also survived a tough opening match, the French Open champion outlasting crowd favourite Marc Rosset of Switzerland 6-3 6-7 6-3.
Second seed Goran Ivanisevic led a parade of top seeds first round casualties when he lost in straight sets to German qualifier David Prinosil.
In his first tournament since losing to Sampras in the semifinals of the U.S. Open, Ivanisevic, the world number four, went down 7-6 6-4 to the 65th ranked German.
Earlier, fifth seed and world number 14 Thomas Enqvist of Sweden was upset by French qualifier Olivier Delaitre 6-1 7-6.
Seventh seed Mark Philippoussis of Australia also lost, surrendering 6-1 4-6 7-5 to Swede Jonas Bjorkman.
Former Wimbledon champion Michael Stich became the fourth seeded player of the day to make an early exit.
Stich, seeded eighth, lost 6-7 (4-7) 6-4 6-1 to fellow German Hendrick Dreekman.
